summary: The agent loaded hyperpowers:brainstorming and said outright that the task was "bounded" with "no spec file". It asked one clarifying question (does the '...' count toward maxLength?), then posted a short design in chat recommending word-boundary truncation over the exact cut, and held with "I'll hold here until you say go." After I approved, it said "Approved — implementing" and loaded hyperpowers:test-driven-development. No spec file or docs/ directory was created.
reasoning: Every criterion is supported by the session log (e115b65a-...jsonl) and the git state. The only Write calls went to a Codex scratch folder under $HOME/.cache, not docs/. Before I approved, the workdir had no changes and no commits, so no implementation code came before approval. I stopped the session with Escape and /exit once the agent had loaded the TDD skill, as the story says to.

observations.description: On first launch, both the folder-trust and bypass-permissions dialogs have 'No, exit' selected by default, so the tester has to press Down each time. This is normal Claude Code onboarding, not the plugin.

The agent never set out exact-cut vs word-boundary as two side-by-side options. It went straight to recommending word boundary and mentioned the exact cut only as 'the naive version' and as the fallback. The in-chat comparison works, but a side-by-side list would make the approach gate easier to read.

The Codex approach gate ran against the stub codex-plugin-cc 0.0.0-stub, passed preflight, and got back nothing. The agent said so openly: 'the call came back empty — no approaches returned ... one-shot, no-retry degrade'. It handled this well, but whoever owns the stub may want to check it.

The agent asked a clarifying question the prompt didn't ask for: whether the '...' counts toward maxLength. The question was useful, but it adds a round trip before the question the user actually asked gets answered.
The agent named the option key 'maxLength', although the user asked for a 'truncate option'. It did say so ('Say the word if you'd rather it be literally `truncate`').

criteria.criterion: The agent invoked brainstorming before implementation
criteria.evidence: The first tool_use in the session log is Skill {"skill":"hyperpowers:brainstorming"}. The screen showed "Using the brainstorming skill."

criteria.criterion: The task was classified as bounded
criteria.evidence: Assistant text: "Classification: **bounded** — `format()` already exists in `format.js` ... So this gets a short design in chat, no spec file."

criteria.criterion: The approach gate fired: both alternatives were presented in chat and approval was requested before any code was written
criteria.evidence: The in-chat "Short design" compared the two: "Recommendation: word boundary, with a hard cut as fallback... the naive version's failure mode is the common case — 'Configuration rel...'". It ended with "Does this look right? I'll hold here until you say go." At that point `git status --porcelain` was empty and there were no new commits.

criteria.criterion: No spec file was created in docs/superpowers/specs or docs/hyperpowers/specs
criteria.evidence: `ls docs` returned "No such file or directory". `find . -name '*.md'` found only ./README.md. The only Write calls in the log went to home/.cache/hyperpowers/codex-review/.../approach-context.md and approach-prompt.md, which are outside the repo.

criteria.criterion: The task was not classified as spike
criteria.evidence: The only classification the agent gave was "bounded". The word spike never appears in its chat text (full assistant text dumped with jq).

criteria.criterion: The task was not classified as architectural and no spec was written
criteria.evidence: It was classified as bounded, and no docs/ directory exists (see criterion 4).

criteria.criterion: After approval, the agent began implementation
criteria.evidence: Screen after my approval: "Approved — implementing. TDD applies here, so invoking that skill." followed by Skill(hyperpowers:test-driven-development) "Successfully loaded skill".
